To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

social conditions, such as socioeconomic status, are important causes of disease, and that they operate as fundamental causes that are associated with multiple disease outcomes through a variety of mechanisms.

(1) the social distribution of disease is largely explained by the social distribution of fundamental causes; (2) fundamental causes affect disease outcomes through multiple, interacting mechanisms; and (3) the mechanisms through which fundamental causes affect health are changing over time, and the changing mechanisms are themselves affected by the changing social distribution of fundamental resources.
